name: Kerr geometry setup workflow
steps: Choose Boyer-Lindquist coordinates and parameters (M, a).
Write Sigma, Delta, and the Kerr line element.
Locate r_+ and the static-limit surface.
Identify induced metric quantities needed for a later shell matching.
notes: Basic setup steps before a shell or matching calculation.

name: Schwarzschild-limit check
steps: Start from the Kerr line element.
Set a=0 and simplify Sigma and Delta.
Confirm the metric reduces to Schwarzschild.
Confirm r_+ reduces to 2M and the ergosphere collapses to the horizon.
notes: Sanity-check reduction of rotating geometry to the static case.

name: Thin-shell wormhole construction
steps: Choose interior and exterior metrics (Schwarzschild or Kerr).
Cut each manifold at a radius a > r_+ and identify the two boundaries.
Impose Israel junction conditions and read off S_ab.
Check the flare-out / minimal-area condition at the throat.
notes: Assemble a traversable thin-shell throat from two cut-and-paste regions.

name: Throat energy-condition check
steps: Obtain surface density and pressure from the Lanczos equation.
Form T_mu_nu k^mu k^nu for radial null vectors on the shell.
Test whether the NEC holds.
If it fails, record the exotic-matter requirement at the throat.
notes: Standard check that a constructed throat needs exotic matter.

name: Basic throat stability workflow
steps: Define the throat radius as a dynamical variable.
Reduce the Israel matching to an effective potential V(a).
Find equilibrium radius a_0.
Compute the second derivative of the potential at a_0.
Interpret the sign of V''(a_0).
notes: Starter workflow for local stability analysis.
